30: Maya's family is moving today and the whole street can see it. Two men are carrying the sofa down the stairs very slowly. Her father is rolling up the carpet, her mother is taking down the curtains, and Maya is holding a mirror and trying not to look at herself. Diego is filming everything for Radio Aurora. Nobody is finding the lamp. What is happening in your house right now? Describe it as you watch!
31: Last month Oliver broke his arm skating. First they took an X-ray, then the doctor put his arm in plaster, and he stayed in hospital for one night. Two days later everybody visited him with comics, and a week later he was playing the guitar with one hand — badly, but happily. The nurse said he was the noisiest patient of the year. What happened to YOU last year? Tell it in order!
32: Kili has brought postcards from five different countries in one week, and nobody knows how. This one has got a beautiful stamp and an address in tiny letters. That one was sent from a mountain village and arrived three months late. Ingrid reads them all out loud: the weather, the food, the sea. Then she writes one back. Who would YOU send a postcard to? Write it!
33: Saturday is free! How about tennis? says Ingrid. Diego prefers the cinema. Shall we go to the beach instead? Maybe — but the forecast says rain. Let's decide by lunchtime, then. They suggest six different plans, agree on none of them, and end up doing the best thing of all: nothing, together, by the sea. How about YOUR Saturday? Suggest a plan to a friend!
34: Oliver! Your new speaker is TOO loud — my experiment is shaking! shouts Maya from the other room. It's not loud enough, answers Oliver. The box is too heavy to move, the volume button is too small to find and the instructions are too difficult to read. Maya is not patient enough for any of this today. Is your bag too heavy? Say what is too much and what is not enough!
35: When I'm sad, I play my guitar, says Oliver. When I'm happy, I play it louder — much louder. When Kili is angry, he sits on the roof and refuses to speak to anybody for hours. When Ingrid is worried, she makes lists; when Maya is surprised, she takes notes instead of screaming. And when everybody is proud, they celebrate together by the sea. What do YOU do when you're sad or happy? Say it with when!
36: English mystery, investigated by Maya and Ingrid: you MAKE a cake but you DO the dishes. You make your bed, you make a mistake, you make a noise. You do your homework, you do the shopping, you do your best. Why? Nobody knows — but everybody has to learn it. Ingrid writes two lists on the wall. Make or do? Choose the right one for each thing you do today!
37: New series on Radio Aurora: secret hobbies! Diego discovers that the maths teacher collects old comics, that Oliver plays chess online at midnight, and that the school cook is famous for her photography. Diego himself enjoys cooking but he doesn't like eating what he cooks. What do YOU love doing in your free time? Come on the radio and tell everybody!
38: Big news: the city TV channel wants a report about our school! Diego is delighted, obviously. He thinks documentaries are more interesting than cartoons; Kili strongly disagrees and says cartoons are clearly superior. They watch the programme together on a tiny screen and argue happily all afternoon. What kind of programmes do YOU like? Give your opinion and defend it!
39: Every great expedition learns from the past. Maya tells the class about explorers who crossed oceans in wooden ships, who drew the first maps of coasts nobody had seen, and who climbed mountains without modern equipment. Some discovered new places; many simply came home and wrote everything down. Ingrid takes notes. Which explorer would YOU like to be? Tell their story in the past!
40: Question of the week: what was the best day of your life? For Oliver it was the first concert, with the worst sound and the biggest happiness. For Ingrid it was the day the expedition started. The funniest day was the pizza disaster; the most beautiful, the night of the northern lights. Nobody agrees, and that is the point. What was YOUR best day ever?
41: Special report by Diego and Maya: our town, fifty years ago and today! The old photos show a smaller town, quieter and emptier, with one shop and no traffic lights. Today it is bigger, noisier and much more crowded, but there is also a new library and a park. Is the modern town better than the ancient one? Compare YOUR town then and now — and decide!
42: The school phone rang six times today and one call was very strange. Hello, can I speak to the director, please? Could you hold on a moment? said Kili, who should never answer a phone. He took a message, lost it, found it, and read it upside down. One caller had the wrong number and stayed talking for ten minutes anyway. Can YOU answer the phone in English? Practise it!
43: Summer plans! We're going to stay one night in each place, says Ingrid, reading her list: a hotel in the city, a tent by the lake, an old caravan on the farm and — the best one — a real lighthouse by the sea. Maya is going to pack one small suitcase; Ingrid is going to pack four. They aren't going to be bored for a single minute. Where are YOU going to go this summer?
44: The funfair came to town! Oliver rode the roller coaster three times and lost his voice on the second. Diego bought the tickets, stood in the longest queue, ate candy floss and gave a balloon to a small child who cried anyway. They went on the big wheel at sunset and saw the whole town. They came home late and slept for ten hours. What did YOU do at the funfair?
45: Kili found an old bottle on the beach with a REAL map inside! Ingrid unfolds it carefully: go north from the harbour, then east along the cliffs, then south at the third rock, and dig where the two paths cross. West of that point there is only the sea. They walk all afternoon and find… another bottle, with another map. Can YOU follow directions? Grab a compass!
46: I might be a scientist, says Maya, or a vet — or a scientist who studies vets. I may work at sea, or I may not. Oliver is completely sure: he might be a musician, he might be a farmer, and he sees no problem with being both. Nothing is decided yet, and perhaps that is the best part. What might YOU be in the future? Nothing is certain — say it with might!
47: Every good captain has a plan B. If it rains on Saturday, we'll do the quiz inside, says Ingrid, writing on the board. If it's sunny, we'll have the picnic by the lake and swim before lunch. If the bus is late, we'll walk. And if Kili delivers the invitations on time, everybody will come — which is the biggest 'if' of all. What will you do if it rains this weekend? Make your own plan A and plan B!
48: Riddle time with Maya and Diego! A person who flies and carries letters. A place where ships stop. A thing which tells you the time. A person who cures animals; a place where you borrow books; a thing which you use to see far away. Diego invents one that nobody can solve, including himself. Write your own riddle with who, which and where — and test your class!
49: Welcome to QUICK ANSWERS, the game show where long answers lose points! Do you like maths? Yes, I do. Has she got a bike? No, she hasn't. Were they at the concert? Yes, they were. Diego answers correctly but adds three sentences of explanation every time, so Ingrid wins easily. Short and correct — that's the rule. Ready? Answer quickly and get the point!
50: Music tip from Oliver: it's not only WHAT you play, it's HOW you play it. Play this part slowly, that part quickly. Sing quietly here, loudly there, and always finish well. Maya listens carefully and writes every instruction down neatly in her notebook. Then Oliver plays the last note badly on purpose, and the whole room laughs. How do you do things — carefully, fast, well? Add the adverb and say it properly!
51: The examiner will ask about YOU, says Diego, so let's practise. What's your surname? How do you spell it? How old are you? Where are you from? What's your favourite subject? Have you got any brothers or sisters? What do you do at the weekend? Kili answers everything about himself, in detail, for eleven minutes. Answer these questions about you — clearly and calmly!
52: Word Games Championship! Six rounds, two teams and one enormous dictionary as referee. Round one: spelling. Round two: find the vowels. Round three: which word has this sound? Ingrid's team is faster, Oliver's team is louder, and the dictionary settles two arguments. In the last round, a single letter decides everything. Do you remember the words of the whole course? Choose your team and start playing!
53: Listening exam secrets from Kili and Maya: read the questions BEFORE the recording starts, because then you know what to wait for. You will hear everything twice — don't panic the first time. Write in pencil, check the example, and never leave a gap empty. Kili adds his own rule: don't fly around during the exam. Ready to listen? Sharpen your pencil!
54: Reading & Writing: 40 minutes, 7 parts. The golden rules, by Ingrid and Diego: read the title first, because it tells you what the text is about. Underline the important words in each question. Copy exactly — spelling counts, and so do capital letters. Never leave anything blank, and always check the number of words at the end. Take a deep breath: you know more than you think!
55: Fifty-five units, hundreds of words, one amazing team. The Aurora graduation ceremony begins at six: certificates on the table, the hall full of families, and Kili — who has never been on time in his life — waiting at the door with the diplomas. Ingrid, Diego, Maya and Oliver remember every adventure, from the first suitcase to this evening. They are proud. And so should YOU be. Congratulations, explorer!
